sanskrit: evam uktas tu rāmeṇa parāṃ vrīḍām upāgataḥ śatrughno vīryasaṃpanno mandaṃ mandam uvāca ha
english: Thus addressed by Rāma, Śatrughna—endowed with heroic valour—was overcome by deep embarrassment and spoke slowly, word by word.

sanskrit: avaśyaṃ karaṇīyaṃ ca śāsanaṃ puruṣarṣabha tava caiva mahābhāga śāsanaṃ duratikramam ayaṃ kāmakaro rājaṃs tavāsmi puruṣarṣabha
english: "O bull among men, your command must certainly be carried out; O greatly blessed one, your command is impossible to transgress. I am your willing servant, O king, O bull among men."

sanskrit: evam ukte tu śūreṇa śatrughnena mahātmanā uvāca rāmaḥ saṃhṛṣṭo lakṣmaṇaṃ bharataṃ tathā
english: When the heroic and great-souled Śatrughna had spoken thus, the delighted Rāma addressed Lakṣmaṇa and Bharata.

sanskrit: saṃbhārān abhiṣekasya ānayadhvaṃ samāhitāḥ adyaiva puruṣavyāghram abhiṣekṣyāmi durjayam
english: "Bring with careful attention the materials for the consecration; today itself I shall consecrate this tiger among men, this invincible hero."

sanskrit: purodhasaṃ ca kākutsthau naigamān ṛtvijas tathā mantriṇaś caiva me sarvān ānayadhvaṃ mamājñayā
english: "O ye two of Kākutstha's line, by my command summon the chief priest, the city elders, the officiating priests, and all my ministers."

sanskrit: rājñaḥ śāsanam ājñāya tathākurvan mahārathāḥ abhiṣekasamārambhaṃ puraskṛtya purodhasaṃ praviṣṭā rājabhavanaṃ puraṃdaragṛhopamam
english: Knowing the king's command, the great chariot-warriors acted accordingly; placing the chief priest at their head and setting the consecration rites in motion, they entered the royal palace, which resembled the abode of Indra.

sanskrit: tato 'bhiṣeko vavṛdhe śatrughnasya mahātmanaḥ saṃpraharṣakaraḥ śrīmān rāghavasya purasya ca
english: Then the auspicious consecration of the great-souled Śatrughna grew in grandeur, bringing great rejoicing to Rāghava's city.

sanskrit: tato 'bhiṣiktaṃ śatrughnam aṅkam āropya rāghavaḥ uvāca madhurāṃ vāṇīṃ tejas tasyābhipūrayan
english: Then, seating the consecrated Śatrughna upon his lap, Rāghava spoke sweet words to him, filling him with radiant energy.

sanskrit: ayaṃ śaras tv amoghas te divyaḥ parapuraṃjayaḥ anena lavaṇaṃ saumya hantāsi raghunandana
english: "This arrow of yours is unfailing and divine, the conqueror of enemy citadels; with this, O gentle one, O delight of Raghu's line, you shall slay Lavaṇa."

sanskrit: sṛṣṭaḥ śaro 'yaṃ kākutstha yadā śete mahārṇave svayambhūr ajito devo yaṃ nāpaśyan surāsurāḥ
english: "This arrow, O Kākutstha, was fashioned when the self-born, unconquered god lay upon the great ocean—he whom neither gods nor asuras could behold."

sanskrit: adṛśyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ tenāyaṃ hi śarottamaḥ sṛṣṭaḥ krodhābhibhūtena vināśārthaṃ durātmanoḥ madhukaiṭabhayor vīra vighāte vartamānayoḥ
english: "Invisible to all creatures, he—when overcome by wrath for the destruction of those two evil-souled ones, Madhu and Kaiṭabha, who were engaged in wreaking havoc—fashioned this supreme arrow, O hero."

sanskrit: sraṣṭukāmena lokāṃs trīṃs tau cānena hatau yudhi anena śaramukhyena tato lokāṃś cakāra saḥ
english: "Desiring to create the three worlds, he slew those two in battle with this weapon; with this foremost of arrows, he then brought the worlds into being."

sanskrit: nāyaṃ mayā śaraḥ pūrvaṃ rāvaṇasya vadhārthinā muktaḥ śatrughna bhūtānāṃ mahāṃs trāso bhaved iti
english: "This arrow was not released by me earlier when I sought to slay Rāvaṇa, O Śatrughna, lest great terror befall all creatures."

sanskrit: yac ca tasya mahac chūlaṃ tryambakeṇa mahātmanā dattaṃ śatruvināśāya madhor āyudham uttamam
english: "And there is that great trident given by the mighty three-eyed god for the destruction of enemies—Madhu's supreme weapon."

sanskrit: tat saṃnikṣipya bhavane pūjyamānaṃ punaḥ punaḥ diśaḥ sarvāḥ samālokya prāpnoty āhāram ātmanaḥ
english: "Having stored that weapon in his dwelling, worshipping it again and again, he ranges in all directions, surveying them, and thereby obtains food for himself."

sanskrit: yadā tu yuddham ākāṅkṣan kaś cid enaṃ samāhvayet tadā śūlaṃ gṛhītvā tad bhasma rakṣaḥ karoti tam
english: "But when someone challenges him, desiring battle, then the rākṣasa seizes that trident and reduces the challenger to ashes."

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ puruṣaśārdūla tam āyudhavivarjitam apraviṣṭapuraṃ pūrvaṃ dvāri tiṣṭha dhṛtāyudhaḥ
english: "Therefore, O tiger among men, before he re-enters his citadel and while he is without his weapon, stand at the gateway bearing your arms."

sanskrit: apraviṣṭaṃ ca bhavanaṃ yuddhāya puruṣarṣabha āhvayethā mahābāho tato hantāsi rākṣasaṃ
english: "And when he has not yet entered his dwelling, O bull among men, O mighty-armed one, challenge him to battle; then you shall slay the rākṣasa."

sanskrit: anyathā kriyamāṇe tu avadhyaḥ sa bhaviṣyati yadi tv evaṃ kṛte vīra vināśam upayāsyati
english: "If it is done otherwise, he will be invincible; but if it is done in this manner, O hero, he will meet his destruction."

sanskrit: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ śūlasya ca viparyayam śrīmataḥ śitikaṇṭhasya kṛtyaṃ hi duratikramam
english: "All this has been explained to you, including the counter to the trident; for the deed of the glorious blue-throated one is impossible to transgress."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu kākutsthaṃ praśasya ca punaḥ punaḥ punar evāparaṃ vākyam uvāca raghunandanaḥ
english: Having spoken thus to Kākutstha and praised him again and again, the delight of Raghu's line spoke yet further words.

sanskrit: imāny aśvasahasrāṇi catvāri puruṣarṣabha rathānāṃ ca sahasre dve gajānāṃ śatam eva ca
english: "O bull among men, four thousand horses, two thousand chariots, and a hundred elephants—"

sanskrit: antarāpaṇavīthyaś ca nānāpaṇyopaśobhitāḥ anugacchantu śatrughna tathaiva naṭanartakāḥ
english: "—and market convoys adorned with goods of every kind, and likewise entertainers and dancers, let them accompany you, Śatrughna."

sanskrit: hiraṇyasya suvarṇasya ayutaṃ puruṣarṣabha gṛhītvā gaccha śatrughna paryāptadhanavāhanaḥ
english: "Taking ten thousand pieces of silver and gold, go forth, O Śatrughna, O bull among men, abundantly supplied with wealth and conveyances."

sanskrit: balaṃ ca subhṛtaṃ vīra hṛṣṭapuṣṭam anuttamam saṃbhāṣya saṃpradānena rañjayasva narottama
english: "And the army, well-maintained, joyful, and well-fed, unsurpassed—O foremost of men, please and gratify them with kind words and generous gifts."

sanskrit: na hy arthās tatra tiṣṭhanti na dārā na ca bāndhavāḥ suprīto bhṛtyavargas tu yatra tiṣṭhati rāghava
english: "For wealth does not abide there, nor wife, nor kinsmen—O Rāghava, only the corps of well-gratified servants endures."

sanskrit: ato hṛṣṭajanākīrṇāṃ prasthāpya mahatīṃ camūm eka eva dhanuṣpānis tad gaccha tvaṃ madhor vanam
english: "Therefore, having dispatched that great army thronging with rejoicing men, go you alone, bow in hand, to the forest of Madhu."

sanskrit: yathā tvāṃ na prajānāti gacchantaṃ yuddhakāṅkṣiṇam lavaṇas tu madhoḥ putras tathā gaccher aśaṅkitaḥ
english: "So that Lavaṇa, son of Madhu, does not recognise you as you approach, seeking battle, go without arousing suspicion."

sanskrit: na tasya mṛtyur anyo 'sti kaś cid dhi puruṣarṣabha darśanaṃ yo 'bhigaccheta sa vadhyo lavaṇena hi
english: "For no other death exists for him, O bull among men; whoever comes to face him is surely slain by Lavaṇa."

sanskrit: sa grīṣme vyapayāte tu varṣarātra upasthite hanyās tvaṃ lavaṇaṃ saumya sa hi kālo 'sya durmateḥ
english: "When the summer has passed and the rainy season is at hand, then slay Lavaṇa, O gentle one; for that is the time of this evil-minded one's vulnerability."

sanskrit: maharṣīṃs tu puraskṛtya prayāntu tava sainikāḥ yathā grīṣmāvaśeṣeṇa tareyur jāhnavījalam
english: "Let your soldiers march with great sages at their head, so that with what remains of the summer season they may cross the waters of the Jāhnavī."

sanskrit: tataḥ sthāpya balaṃ sarvaṃ nadītīre samāhitaḥ agrato dhanuṣā sārdhaṃ gaccha tvaṃ laghuvikrama
english: "Then, having stationed all the forces on the riverbank with composure, go forward yourself with bow in hand, O swift-striding one."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu rāmeṇa śatrughnas tān mahābalān senāmukhyān samānīya tato vākyam uvāca ha
english: Thus instructed by Rāma, Śatrughna summoned those mighty commanders of the army and then addressed them with these words.

sanskrit: ete vo gaṇitā vāsā yatra yatra nivatsyatha sthātavyaṃ cāvirodhena yathā bādhā na kasya cit
english: "These are your designated halting places, wherever you shall encamp; you must conduct yourselves without causing obstruction, so that no one is harassed."

sanskrit: tathā tāṃs tu samājñāpya niryāpya ca mahad balam kausalyāṃ ca sumitrāṃ ca kaikeyīṃ cābhyavādayat
english: Having given them such instruction and sent the great army forth, he paid his respects to Kausalyā, Sumitrā, and Kaikeyī.

sanskrit: rāmaṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā śirasābhipraṇamya ca rāṇeṇa cābhyanujñātaḥ śatrughnaḥ śatrutāpanaḥ
english: Having circumambulated Rāma with reverential right-hand salutation and bowed his head to him, and having been given leave by his lord, Śatrughna the afflicitor of enemies—

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇaṃ bharataṃ caiva praṇipatya kṛtāñjaliḥ purodhasaṃ vasiṣṭhaṃ ca śatrughnaḥ prayatātmavān pradakṣiṇam atho kṛtvā nirjagāma mahābalaḥ
english: —Śatrughna, of disciplined spirit and mighty strength, prostrated himself with joined palms before Lakṣmaṇa and Bharata, and then, having circumambulated the chief priest Vasiṣṭha, departed.

sanskrit: prasthāpya tad balaṃ sarvaṃ māsamātroṣitaḥ pathi eka evāśu śatrughno jagāma tvaritas tadā
english: Having dispatched that entire army and himself halting only a month along the road, Śatrughna then went forward swiftly and alone with haste.

sanskrit: dvirātram antare śūra uṣya rāghavanandanaḥ vālmīker āśramaṃ puṇyam agacchad vāsam uttamam
english: After halting for two nights along the way, the hero and delight of Raghu's line came to the holy hermitage of Vālmīki, that most excellent of abodes.

sanskrit: so 'bhivādya mahātmānaṃ vālmīkiṃ munisattamam kṛtāñjalir atho bhūtvā vākyam etad uvāca ha
english: He greeted the great-souled Vālmīki, that foremost of sages, and then, standing with joined palms, spoke these words.

sanskrit: bhagavan vastum icchāmi guroḥ kṛtyād ihāgataḥ śvaḥ prabhāte gamiṣyāmi pratīcīṃ vāruṇīṃ diśam
english: "O venerable one, I wish to stay here tonight; I have come hither on a task for my lord, and at dawn tomorrow I shall proceed toward the western quarter, the domain of Varuṇa."

sanskrit: śatrughnasya vacaḥ śrutvā prahasya munipuṃgavaḥ pratyuvāca mahātmānaṃ svāgataṃ te mahāyaśaḥ
english: Hearing Śatrughna's words, that bull among sages smiled and replied to the great-souled one: "Welcome to you, O greatly renowned one."

sanskrit: svam āśramam idaṃ saumya rāghavāṇāṃ kulasya ha āsanaṃ pādyam arghyaṃ ca nirviśaṅkaḥ pratīccha me
english: "This hermitage is verily the home of the Rāghava lineage, O gentle one; accept without hesitation the seat, the water for feet, and the guest-offering that I extend."

sanskrit: pratigṛhya tataḥ pūjāṃ phalamūlaṃ ca bhojanam bhakṣayām āsa kākutsthas tṛptiṃ ca paramāṃ gataḥ
english: Then Kākutstha accepted the honour and ate the food of fruits and roots, and was filled with utmost satisfaction.

sanskrit: sa tu bhuktvā mahābāhur maharṣiṃ tam uvāca ha pūrvaṃ yajñavibhūtīyaṃ kasyāśramasamīpataḥ
english: Having eaten, the mighty-armed one then asked the great sage: "In former times, to whose hermitage near here did the splendour of the sacrifice belong?"

sanskrit: tasya tadbhāṣitaṃ śrutvā vālmīkir vākyam abravīt śatrughna śṛṇu yasyedaṃ babhūvāyatanaṃ purā
english: Hearing that question of his, Vālmīki spoke these words: "O Śatrughna, listen—learn to whom this sacred precinct formerly belonged."

sanskrit: yuṣmākaṃ pūrvako rājā sudāsasya mahātmanaḥ putro mitrasaho nāma vīryavān atidhārmikaḥ
english: "An ancestor of your line, the son of the great-souled Sudāsa, named Mitrasaha—valiant and supremely righteous—"

sanskrit: sa bāla eva saudāso mṛgayām upacakrame cañcūryamāṇaṃ dadṛśe sa śūro rākṣasadvayam
english: "—this Saudāsa, even as a youth, took to the hunt; and the hero beheld a pair of rākṣasas prowling about."

sanskrit: śārdūlarūpiṇau ghorau mṛgān bahusahasraśaḥ bhakṣayāṇāv asaṃtuṣṭau paryāptiṃ ca na jagmatuḥ
english: "Terrible in the form of tigers, they were devouring many thousands of deer and yet were not satisfied, never reaching fullness."

sanskrit: sa tu tau rākṣasau dṛṣṭvā nirmṛgaṃ ca vanaṃ kṛtam krodhena mahatāviṣṭo jaghānaikaṃ maheṣuṇā
english: "Seeing those two rākṣasas and finding the forest stripped of deer, he was seized by great wrath and slew one of them with a mighty arrow."

sanskrit: vinipātya tam ekaṃ tu saudāsaḥ puruṣarṣabhaḥ vijvaro vigatāmarṣo hataṃ rakṣo 'bhyavaikṣata
english: "Having struck down that one, Saudāsa the bull among men, his fever of rage spent and his fury gone, looked upon the slain rākṣasa."

sanskrit: nirīkṣamāṇaṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā sahāyas tasya rakṣasaḥ saṃtāpam akarod ghoraṃ saudāsaṃ cedam abravīt
english: "Seeing him gazing thus, the companion of that rākṣasa was filled with terrible anguish and spoke these words to Saudāsa:"

sanskrit: yasmād anaparāddhaṃ tvaṃ sahāyaṃ mama jaghnivān tasmāt tavāpi pāpiṣṭha pradāsyāmi pratikriyām
english: "'Because you have slain my companion who had committed no offence, therefore, O most wicked one, I shall repay you in kind.'"

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu taṃ rakṣas tatraivāntaradhīyata kālaparyāyayogena rājā mitrasaho 'bhavat
english: "Having spoken thus, that rākṣasa vanished on the spot; and in the course of time King Mitrasaha came to reign."

sanskrit: rājāpi yajate yajñaṃ tasyāśramasamīpataḥ aśvamedhaṃ mahāyajñaṃ taṃ vasiṣṭho 'bhyapālayat
english: "The king too performed a sacrifice—the great Aśvamedha sacrifice—near that hermitage; Vasiṣṭha supervised that ritual."

sanskrit: tatra yajño mahān āsīd bahuvarṣagaṇāyutān samṛddhaḥ parayā lakṣmyā devayajñasamo 'bhavat
english: "There the great sacrifice lasting for many years and groups of years prospered with the highest splendour and was the equal of a sacrifice of the gods."

sanskrit: athāvasāne yajñasya pūrvavairam anusmaran vasiṣṭharūpī rājānam iti hovāca rākṣasaḥ
english: "Then, at the close of the sacrifice, remembering his former enmity, the rākṣasa assumed the form of Vasiṣṭha and thus addressed the king:"

sanskrit: adya yajñāvasānānte sāmiṣaṃ bhojanaṃ mama dīyatām iti śīghraṃ vai nātra kāryā vicāraṇā
english: "'At the conclusion of the sacrifice today, let food containing meat be given to me quickly—there is to be no deliberation in this matter.'"

sanskrit: tac chrutvā vyāhṛtaṃ vākyaṃ rakṣasā kāmarūpiṇā bhakṣasaṃskārakuśalam uvāca pṛthivīpatiḥ
english: "Hearing those words spoken by the rākṣasa who could take any form at will, the lord of the earth—skilled in the preparation of food—addressed his cook:"

sanskrit: haviṣyaṃ sāmiṣaṃ svādu yathā bhavati bhojanam tathā kuruṣva śīghraṃ vai parituṣyed yathā guruḥ
english: "'Prepare quickly a dish of oblation-food containing meat so as to be tasty, in such a way that the guru may be well pleased.'"

sanskrit: śāsanāt pārthivendrasya sūdaḥ saṃbhrāntamānasaḥ sa ca rakṣaḥ punas tatra sūdaveṣam athākarot
english: "At the command of the lord of kings, the cook—his mind agitated—went about his task; and that rākṣasa there again took on the disguise of the cook."

sanskrit: sa mānuṣam atho māṃsaṃ pārthivāya nyavedayat idaṃ svāduhaviṣyaṃ ca sāmiṣaṃ cānnam āhṛtam
english: "He then presented human flesh to the king, announcing: 'This tasty oblation-food with meat has been brought.'"

sanskrit: sa bhojanaṃ vasiṣṭhāya patnyā sārdham upāharat madayantyā naravyāghra sāmiṣaṃ rakṣasā hṛtam
english: "He brought that food—tampered with by the rākṣasa, O tiger among men—to present to Vasiṣṭha together with his wife Madayantī."

sanskrit: jñātvā tadāmiṣaṃ vipro mānuṣaṃ bhojanāhṛtam krodhena mahatāviṣṭo vyāhartum upacakrame
english: "The brahmin, knowing that the food brought was human flesh, was seized by great wrath and began to utter a curse."

sanskrit: yasmāt tvaṃ bhojanaṃ rājan mamaitad dātum icchasi tasmād bhojanam etat te bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ
english: "'Because you, O king, wish to give me this as food, therefore this food shall be yours—there is no doubt of this.'"

sanskrit: sa rājā saha patnyā vai praṇipatya muhur muhuḥ punar vasiṣṭhaṃ provāca yad uktaṃ brahmarūpiṇā
english: "That king, together with his wife, prostrated himself again and again and then explained to Vasiṣṭha what had been said by one who had assumed the form of a brahmin."

sanskrit: tac chrutā pārthivendrasya rakṣasā vikṛtaṃ ca tat punaḥ provāca rājānaṃ vasiṣṭhaḥ puruṣarṣabham
english: "Having heard the account of the lord of kings and that the matter had been distorted by the rākṣasa, Vasiṣṭha again addressed the king, that bull among men:"

sanskrit: mayā roṣaparītena yad idaṃ vyāhṛtaṃ vacaḥ naitac chakyaṃ vṛthā kartuṃ pradāsyāmi ca te varam
english: "'This word I have uttered in the grip of rage cannot be made void; yet I shall grant you a boon:"

sanskrit: kālo dvādaśa varṣāṇi śāpasyāsya bhaviṣyati matprasādāc ca rājendra atītaṃ na smariṣyasi
english: "'The duration of this curse shall be twelve years; and by my grace, O lord of kings, you shall not remember what has passed.'"

sanskrit: evaṃ sa rājā taṃ śāpam upabhujyārimardanaḥ pratilebhe punā rājyaṃ prajāś caivānvapālayat
english: "Thus that king, the crusher of enemies, having endured that curse, regained his kingdom and thereafter protected his subjects."

sanskrit: tasya kalmāṣapādasya yajñasyāyatanaṃ śubham āśramasya samīpe 'smin yasmin pṛcchasi rāghava
english: "This auspicious precinct of the sacrifice of that Kalmāṣapāda is the one near this hermitage about which you ask, O Rāghava."

sanskrit: tasya tāṃ pārthivendrasya kathāṃ śrutvā sudāruṇām viveśa parṇaśālāyāṃ maharṣim abhivādya ca
english: "Having heard that most terrible story of that lord of kings, and having paid his respects to the great sage, he entered the leaf-hut."
